seo.title: Washington, D.C. Homeless Help - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified shelter, food, health, employment, benefits, legal aid, and other help for people experiencing homelessness in Washington, D.C.

notice.text: Call ahead when possible. A listing does not guarantee a bed, appointment, meal, service, job, benefit, or approval. Shelter is first come, first served unless a program says otherwise. If you have nowhere to sleep tonight, start with

content.text: is a lightweight, open-source directory. It is not an emergency service and does not operate the organizations listed.
If you need a place tonight, call the Shelter Hotline first.

DC low-barrier shelters accept people on a first-come, first-served basis. The hotline can check current options and arrange free, accessible transport. It cannot promise that a bed will still be available when you arrive.

items.name: DC Shelter Hotline and street outreach

content.text: daily, 8 a.m. to midnight; 24 hours from November 1 through March 31.

shelter information, wellness checks, outreach, blankets or water when available, and free accessible transport to shelter or a warming site. Outreach normally operates Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., with longer hours during cold-weather activations.
2722 Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue SE

Adults can go directly, but call the Shelter Hotline before traveling when possible. These sites are open 24 hours according to the current DC list. Entry is first come, first served; no bed is guaranteed.
6010 Georgia Avenue NW; normally 7 p.m. to 7 a.m.
Entry is first come, first served. Harriet Tubman provides shelter, meals, showers, toiletries, and referrals. Call the Shelter Hotline for current capacity and transport.

items.name: Living Life Alternatives - LGBTQ+ low-barrier shelter

content.text: 24-hour low-barrier shelter for LGBTQ+ adults. Call the shelter or Shelter Hotline before traveling when possible; space is not guaranteed.

items.name: Virginia Williams Family Resource Center - families

content.text: 64 New York Avenue NE, 1st Floor, Washington, DC

Central assessment and referral point for families with children seeking emergency shelter and housing help. Family shelter placements are made through intake; family shelter buildings are not walk-in sites. Call before going and bring household documents if you have them. After hours, call the Shelter Hotline.
, open 24 hours for emergency shelter and support.
Covenant House The Sanctuary, 511 Mellon Street SE,

items.name: Central Union Mission - men's overnight shelter

content.text: daily at 3 p.m., first come, first served. Capacity is limited. The Mission also provides meals and longer-term programs.

From November 1 through March 31, the Shelter Hotline operates 24 hours. Additional hypothermia sites open as the system approaches capacity. During an Extreme Cold Alert, open sites may extend to 24-hour operation.
Do not wait for symptoms of hypothermia.

Meal times and pantry stock can change, especially on holidays. Arrive early and call first when possible. Some meals require no identification, while grocery programs may ask for DC residency or household information.
breakfast daily, 7:30 to 8:30 a.m.; lunch daily, 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.

items.name: Bread for the City - monthly groceries

content.text: Monday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. Groceries are generally available once a month and are based on household size. Friday free farmers markets alternate by location.

items.name: St. Maria's Meals - Wednesday takeaway meal

content.text: outside Catholic Charities, 924 G Street NW
Wednesday, 5 to 6 p.m. No registration or application is required.

items.name: McKenna's Wagon - free evening meals every day

content.text: New Jersey Avenue and I Street NW, approximately 5:15 to 5:40 p.m.
19th and H Street NW, approximately 6 to 6:25 p.m.
Warm meals, sandwiches, fruit, and drinks, 365 days a year at no cost. Times can shift with traffic.
Weekday breakfast and morning guest services, plus an afternoon meal. The schedule has changed before; call or check the official site before traveling.

items.name: N Street Village - meals for women

content.text: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Breakfast is normally 8:45 to 9:45 a.m.; hot lunch is noon to 1 p.m. Serves adult women and people who identify as women.
approximately 5 p.m. Walk-ins are served; call first for holiday changes.
Tuesday and Thursday, 6:30 to 9:30 a.m.; Saturday, 8 to 10 a.m. Food and basic supplies are provided while available.
DC Hunger Solutions maintains a ward-by-ward list of emergency food programs, including schedules and stated identification rules.
These organizations provide practical help. Their faith identity is included so you can make an informed choice. Ask about any optional religious activity before joining a residential program.

St. Maria's Meals, low-barrier shelters, case management, immigration legal help, and other programs. The Wednesday meal states that no registration or application is required; shelter entry rules differ by program.
meals, men's emergency shelter, health care, clothing, employment and social-service connections. Longer residential programs are Christian; ask about expectations before enrolling.

items.name: Charlie's Place at St. Margaret's Episcopal Church

content.text: food, clothing, hygiene items, case management, health referrals, and pantry support. The organization states that it serves people without evangelization.

items.name: Shrine of the Sacred Heart dinner program

content.text: The current local homeless-services directory lists dinner Monday through Saturday, 4 to 5 p.m. Call the parish before traveling because meal schedules can change.
1313 New York Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20005

items.name: Bethany Women's Day Center at N Street Village

showers, laundry, toiletries, meals, wellness, and case management for adult women and people who identify as women. Sign-up is required for showers and laundry.
meals, showers, laundry, toiletries, clothing, lockers, mail, computers, health testing, case management, education, jobs, legal support, and documents for young people facing housing instability.

Adult clothing while stock lasts. SOME says adults do not need identification for clothing. Sizes and supplies vary.
Downtown Day Services Center, Adams Place, and 801 East all list emergency clothing among their services. Ask at reception about current stock and distribution times.
Clothing sign-up is normally Tuesday and Thursday from 6:30 to 7 a.m. The center also distributes toiletries and other essentials while supplies last.

Sasha Bruce Youth Drop-In Center provides clothing to young people. N Street Village's Bethany Day Center provides clothing and basic needs for women. Availability changes; ask before traveling solely for clothing.

categories.title: 6. Medical, mental health, and recovery care

content.text: Call 911 for a medical emergency. Call or text 988 for a mental health, substance use, or suicide crisis. The services below are not emergency departments.

items.name: Unity Health Care for people experiencing homelessness

content.text: Primary care, case management, and other health services at shelters and day centers. Unity accepts patients regardless of ability to pay; free or discounted fees may be available based on income. Walk-in sites include Downtown Day Services Center, Federal City/CCNV, Central Union Mission, Friendship Place, New York Avenue Shelter, N Street Village, and Pathways to Housing. Clinic schedules differ, so call first.

items.name: Unity at Downtown Day Services Center

content.text: 1313 New York Avenue NW, basement suite 1
Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to noon. Walk-in. Confirm before traveling.
Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Walk-in. This is one of Unity's most comprehensive homeless health sites.

items.name: Bread for the City medical clinic

content.text: Primary care for adults and children, examinations, medications, labs, referrals, harm reduction, and coordinated behavioral, dental, and vision care. Care is provided regardless of ability to pay; dental and behavioral programs generally serve established primary-care patients.
Official clinic information and call times
Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; walk-in registration is normally 8 to 11 a.m. Serves adult DC residents and also connects people to mental health and recovery services.
24 hours, 7 days a week. Crisis support, referral to ongoing mental health or substance use care, and activation of mobile crisis teams for people unable or unwilling to travel.

items.name: Community Response Team - crisis response on the street

content.text: 24 hours, 7 days a week. On-the-spot assessment, short-term support, referral, harm-reduction options, and outreach by clinicians and peers.

items.name: DC Stabilization Center - substance use crisis

content.text: 24 hours a day, every day; walk-ins welcome.

free and voluntary for adults 18 or older; no insurance or DC residency required. Services include medical screening and stabilization, peer support, food, clothing, showers, laundry, and connection to longer-term treatment.

items.name: Assessment and Referral Center - treatment enrollment

content.text: Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Call for an appointment or walk in for assessment and referral to detoxification, outpatient, residential, medication-assisted, and recovery services.
Affirming primary care, HIV and sexual health care, behavioral health, insurance navigation, and legal services, with particular expertise serving LGBTQ+ people and people living with HIV.
Downtown Day Services Center, Adams Place, and 801 East provide toilets during open hours. They also offer indoor space and other survival services. Ask staff before leaving belongings unattended.

DC Public Library has 26 locations. The central Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library is at 901 G Street NW. Libraries provide indoor public space, toilets during open hours, computers, Wi-Fi, printing, and scanning. Rules and holiday hours apply.
Downtown Day Services Center, Adams Place, and 801 East list phone charging and computer access. Availability may be limited; bring your own cable and stay with your device.

items.name: Free library computers, Wi-Fi, printing, and scanning

content.text: All DC Public Library locations offer public computers and Wi-Fi. Computer use is first come, first served. The library currently offers up to 20 pages a day of free printing, copying, or scanning.

Library Digital Navigators provide one-to-one help with phones, computers, email, online forms, PDFs, printing, and online privacy at selected branches. Drop-in availability varies; call the branch first.

items.name: Free transport to shelter or warming sites

content.text: Call the DC Shelter Hotline at
. The hotline can arrange free, accessible transport to an available shelter or extreme-weather site. Transport does not reserve a bed.

items.name: Metro Lift - 50% discount for SNAP recipients

content.text: People currently receiving SNAP in DC, Maryland, or Virginia can apply for 50% off Metrobus and Metrorail fares. Enrollment requires an active EBT card, a SmarTrip card, current government photo identification, and a phone number.
Transit Accessibility Center, 655 Virginia Avenue SW, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Walk-ins are welcome.
Metro offers 50% reduced fares for riders age 65 or older and for riders under 65 with qualifying disabilities. The disability program requires an application and Reduced Fare Photo ID.

items.name: District Direct - SNAP, Medicaid, and cash assistance

content.text: Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.

Apply online through District Direct, by paper application, fax, mail, or at a DHS Service Center. Programs include SNAP, Medicaid, TANF, and other cash or medical assistance. Applying does not guarantee eligibility.

items.name: DHS Service Centers - in-person benefits help

content.text: Monday through Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., except holidays.
Anacostia, Fort Davis, Congress Heights, H Street, and Taylor Street. Any center can help; DC uses a no-wrong-door policy. Check the official page for same-day closures before traveling.

Downtown Day Services Center, Adams Place, 801 East, Sasha Bruce Youth Drop-In Center, SOME, and Bread for the City can help people understand or apply for benefits. Ask for a benefits navigator or case manager; assistance and eligibility vary.
Start with a DC day center
Career counseling, resumes, job search and placement, training, labor-market information, and unemployment assistance. Current in-person services may require an appointment.
DCNetworks is the District's job-search system. You can search openings, post a resume, and apply online. Library computers and Digital Navigators can help if you do not have a device.
Occupational training and employment support. Programs have intake requirements and scheduled start dates; call before going.

items.name: Job search at day and youth centers

content.text: Downtown Day Services Center and Adams Place offer employment assistance and computers. Sasha Bruce provides job search and readiness help for young people. N Street Village connects women to training and employment opportunities.

items.name: Washington Legal Clinic for the Homeless

content.text: Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Free legal help with shelter denials, street rights, housing programs, public benefits, identification, discrimination, record sealing, and other civil issues affecting people experiencing homelessness. If you are denied safe, accessible shelter, call this number.
1331 H Street NW, Suite 350; walk-in Tuesday and Thursday, 12:30 to 4 p.m.
1911 Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue SE; walk-in Monday and Thursday, 12:30 to 4 p.m.
Free civil legal services for eligible low-income DC residents. Capacity and case acceptance vary.

items.name: DC Bar Advice and Referral Clinic

content.text: Free Saturday civil legal advice from volunteer attorneys; no appointment. Intake is normally 10 a.m. to noon and capacity is limited. The clinic operates on selected dates, not every Saturday.

Help with health insurance and public-benefit appeals, disability, discrimination, immigration, medical privacy, and name or gender-marker changes. An intake is required; acceptance is not guaranteed. Interpretation, including ASL, is available.

Ayuda provides legal, social, and language services for low-income immigrants in DC, Maryland, and Virginia. Contact the organization for current intake availability; do not pay an unverified person for immigration advice.

items.name: No-fee DC birth certificate and non-driver ID

content.text: Eligible DC residents experiencing homelessness may obtain a no-fee DC birth certificate or non-driver identification card through a DHS-designated access point. A provider must verify eligibility and participation in homeless services; this is not a walk-in fee waiver at every government office.
Downtown Day Services Center, Adams Place, 801 East, Community Connections, Zoe's Doors, Shirley's Place, Latin American Youth Center, SAMU, and Sasha Bruce.
current DC rules require recent HMIS history and documented service engagements. Ask an access-point worker to check eligibility before going to Vital Records or DMV.

items.name: Downtown Day Services Center document help

content.text: Staff can help with vital records and DMV identification vouchers. DMV services are scheduled on site on certain days. Call
Sasha Bruce Youth Drop-In Center helps young people obtain identification and vital records. Zoe's Doors and Latin American Youth Center are also designated ID access points.
Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m.
Clients can use SOME's 71 O Street address and receive a text or email when mail arrives. Identification is required to collect mail. Register before directing important mail there.
Sasha Bruce Youth Drop-In Center at 741 8th Street SE lists mailing services for young people experiencing homelessness or housing instability. Register with staff before using the address.
Washington has very limited public storage for people experiencing homelessness. Do not assume that a shelter will store belongings or accept large bags.

items.name: Adams Place Day Center - limited storage

content.text: The official day-center flyer lists limited storage. Space, duration, and item rules can change. Ask staff in person or call
The youth drop-in center lists lockers among its services. Ask about availability, permitted items, and collection deadlines before leaving anything.

items.name: DC Victim Hotline - domestic violence and crime

content.text: Confidential crisis support and connection to emergency safety, shelter, legal, financial, medical, and emotional resources for victims of crime. If making a call could put you in danger, use a safe device or ask a trusted service provider to help.
Meals, showers, laundry, toiletries, clothing, wellness, case management, housing assessment, health connections, and employment help for adult women and people who identify as women.

items.name: DC youth drop-in centers - up to age 24

content.text: Services vary but may include food, clothing, showers, laundry, case management, health, education, employment, documents, and housing referrals.
Official hours, eligibility, and shelter list
Whitman-Walker provides affirming care, insurance navigation, and free legal intake.

items.name: Ayuda - immigrant legal, social, and language services

content.text: Ayuda supports low-income immigrants in the DC region. Contact the organization directly for current intake. Immigration status can affect eligibility for some benefits, but emergency services may have different rules; ask a qualified provider rather than assuming you cannot apply.

items.name: VA Community Resource and Referral Center - veterans

content.text: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.; last walk-in normally accepted at 3:45 p.m.
Shelter and housing connections, food, health and mental health care, recovery, benefits, employment, and re-entry support for veterans who are homeless or at risk.

items.name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans

content.text: 24 hours, 7 days a week. Free and confidential for veterans who are homeless or at imminent risk, and for family members or supporters calling on their behalf.

items.name: Department of Aging and Community Living

content.text: The Information and Referral unit helps older adults, adults with disabilities, and caregivers find social services, health programs, public benefits, long-term supports, and other assistance.

Tell the Shelter Hotline or a shelter worker if you need an accessible vehicle, mobility accommodation, sign-language access, a service-animal accommodation, or another disability-related change. If safe, describe the specific barrier and keep a record of requests.
If you are denied safe, accessible shelter, call the Washington Legal Clinic for the Homeless at
Ask the Shelter Hotline about current pet and service-animal rules before traveling. A service animal is not the same as a pet; explain any disability-related accommodation you need.

items.name: Humane Rescue Alliance Pet Help Center

content.text: Free pet food and supplies at partner locations, affordable veterinary-care information, behavior support, and crisis resources intended to help people keep their animals. Programs and stock change, so contact the center before traveling.
Lost or found animals, animal emergencies, and information about the current DC animal shelter operator. Call rather than leaving an animal unattended at a facility.
Airports are not shelters. If you are stranded without a safe place to sleep, call the Shelter Hotline before leaving a staffed public area. Metro service does not run all night.
The airport has its own Metrorail station on the Blue and Yellow lines. Use the WMATA trip planner for current service, elevator status, and fare. Metro Lift discounts apply to eligible cards.

The Silver Line serves Dulles Airport. The station connects to the terminal through an indoor pedestrian walkway of roughly five minutes. Train hours and final departures differ by day; check before traveling late at night.

DC uses a decentralized, no-wrong-door coordinated-entry system. A trained provider can assess housing needs and connect eligible people to available programs. An assessment is not a housing offer and does not guarantee placement.
a day center, shelter, street-outreach team, Miriam's Kitchen, Friendship Place, SOME, or another participating provider.
Housing assessment, case management, food, clothing, hygiene items, employment help, and health referrals. Hours differ by day and some services require appointments; call first.

If you still have housing but face eviction, unpaid rent, or unsafe conditions, contact Legal Aid DC or the Washington Legal Clinic promptly. Emergency rental assistance and prevention programs often have funding limits, appointments, and documentation rules; apply before a court date or move-out when possible.
